question.knowledge_point: Estimating a Derivative Given a Graph Using a Backward Difference Approximation
question.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14058551/assets/894d659f3ef4544eeda653f5e098d9ca26f3e06899798441534a1bf395628d0e.png)

The graph of the function $f(x)$ is shown above. 
Approximate ${f}^{′}(x)$ at the point $x=3$ using a backward difference approximation with step size $h=2.$
question.worked_solution:
We use the backward difference approximation formula

$$
{f}^{′}(x)≈\frac{f(x)-f(x-h)}{h},
$$

 
at the point $x=3.$ Applying the above formula with $x=3$ and $h=2$ gives 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(3) & ≈\frac{f(3)-f(3-2)}{2} \\  & =\frac{f(3)-f(1)}{2} \\  & =\frac{0-(-1)}{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
